newsitem.title: PERU: U.S. spy plane flies over Peru siege - sources.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spy plane flies over Peru siege - sources.

text.p: A U.S. spy plane has made several high-altitude night-flights over the site of Peru's hostage siege, gathering information for a possible attack on guerrillas inside, local intelligence sources said on Friday.
They said the plane was a Schweitzer SA-2-37A, equipped with infra-red cameras and used periodically in flights over drug-growing areas in the Peruvian jungle.

"It takes off and goes up using the motor, then the motor is simply switched off and it glides in a circular fashion," one of the sources said. The plane has made two flights over the site in recent days, almost certainly unnoticed by the rebels inside, the sources added.
Although President Alberto Fujimori's government has said it wants to avoid using force to resolve the crisis, it has drawn up plans for a possible storming of the residence as a last resort.

According to anti-terrorism police sources, crack troops were training on Friday at a secret location in Lima around a model of the residence "in case they have to go into the building or repel an attack."
The Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrillas were holding 103 rebels for the 10th day of the crisis on Friday.
